# NJ Black Press Archive

> A historical database of Black publications in New Jersey from 1880 to the present. Maintained by the Center for Cooperative Media at Montclair State University.

## About

The NJ Black Press Archive catalogs 136 Black-owned publications across more than 140 years of New Jersey journalism history. It covers newspapers, magazines, newsletters, and digital outlets across 40+ New Jersey cities from the post-Reconstruction era through today.

Data was curated by Amanda Alicea and led by Cassandra Etienne at the Center for Cooperative Media.

## Access

- Home: https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/
- Full archive: https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/archive.html
- Publication detail: https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/publication.html?id=1 (one page per record, by ID)
- Stories (sourced narratives): https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/story.html
- Eras (one page per decade): https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/era.html
- Publication map: https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/map.html
- Historical notes (guided stories and publication browser): https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/historical-notes.html
- Wiki (one page per publication, cross-linked by city/decade/format): https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/wiki/
- Wiki statistics: https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/wiki/statistics.html
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/CenterCoopMedia/njblackpress

A portable, agent-readable markdown version of the wiki (open knowledge format — one markdown file per record with YAML frontmatter) lives in the repo at `okf/`.

## Data

The complete dataset is available as JSON at:
- https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/data/publications.json
- https://centercoopmedia.github.io/njblackpress/data/featured-publications.json

Each publication record includes: name, city, years of operation, format, frequency, mission statement, key staff, historical notes, archive URLs, and active/ceased status.

## Historical context

This archive documents:
- Black press history spanning post-Reconstruction (1880s) through the digital era
- Publications across Newark, Trenton, Camden, Jersey City, and 40+ other NJ cities
- Key periods: Reconstruction era, Great Migration, Jim Crow era, Civil Rights movement, Black Power era (1967 Newark uprising and aftermath), and contemporary digital journalism
- Publication types: weekly newspapers, monthly magazines, academic journals, community newsletters, digital-native outlets

## Related initiatives

- Black Publishers Collective (BPC): https://centerforcooperativemedia.org/programs/black-publishers-collective/
- South Jersey Information Equity Project (SJIEP): https://sjiep.org
